classification_rule: Only diagnostics containing '[CPLUS-' count as tagged C+ enforcement; plain clang warnings and untagged C+ lowering errors do not. REJECT = check+build fail with [CPLUS-; ACCEPT = both succeed; RUNTIME = compiler cannot prove the violation, so the case is a compile-time capability gap; PARTIAL = check+build fail without any [CPLUS- token.

cases.reason: Constant index 9 into a 2-element vector is statically knowable; C+ only tags constant subscripts of fixed-size C arrays, not indices passed to container methods.
cases.gap: No [CPLUS-BOUNDS] for vector::at_checked(); the runtime API rejects the index (-1, bounds telemetry). Probed separately: the same literal subscript on a local int[3] IS rejected with '[CPLUS-BOUNDS] [CPLUS-SAFE-BOUNDS] array index 9 exceeds length 3'.

cases.reason: drop() releases the owned buffer, so later reads are use-after-free; C+ does not track an 'int *items' field inside a C+ class as a managed owner.
cases.gap: No [CPLUS-LIFETIME]/[CPLUS-OWNER]. Checked accessors report the dead state at runtime; a raw dereference of the stale buffer is silent under --sanitize=none (probed: reads recycled memory).

cases.reason: cplus_move(a) zeroes a and transfers the buffer to b; using a afterwards is a use-after-move.

check.output:
vector_use_after_move.cp:29:38: error: use-after-move: use of moved-from resource 'a'
help: the handle was zeroed by cplus_move

build.output: vector_use_after_move.cp:29:38: error: use-after-move: use of moved-from resource 'a'

cases.gap: The C+ RAII lowering pass DOES reject the use at compile time, but the diagnostic is UNTAGGED (no '[CPLUS-' token) and clang emits no warning, so per the suite rule this is not counted as tagged C+ enforcement. (Diagnostic source location maps to b.drop(); the offending use is a.size().)

cases.reason: Two mutable vector* aliases of one owner permit overlapping mutation; C+ has no aliasing/exclusivity or container-level borrow analysis.
cases.gap: Pointer aliasing compiles cleanly with no [CPLUS-ALIAS]/[CPLUS-BORROW] diagnostic. Copying the owner ('vector b = a;') IS rejected at compile time as 'cannot be copied' (also untagged).

cases.reason: slice s borrows the pre-growth buffer; push_back reallocates and bumps the generation, making s stale. C+ cannot link a returned slice value to its source vector.
cases.gap: No compile-time staleness proof. The library catches it dynamically: stale()==1, valid()==0, at_checked() returns -1.
